category_title: Young adults with intellectual disabilities who exhibit passive agreement and chronic lateness
minimal_context: Michael and his teacher are in a one-on-one goal-setting session to select a self-monitoring tool and establish expectations for being on time.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We need to select a self-monitoring tool to track your behavior and decide on a goal for your classes. Do you want to use the app on your phone or this paper chart?

STUDENT: I will use the paper chart. I am concerned about using my phone during classes.

TUTOR: Okay, we will use the paper chart. What do you think would be an appropriate replacement behavior for you to track?

STUDENT: Being on time.

TUTOR: Alright, being on time. What should our goal be for that?

STUDENT: I want to set a goal of being on time for all of my classes.

options.A: Treat the student's avoidance strategies as compensations rather than refusals to comply with the expected task.
options.B: Provide training that involves modeling or offering examples and non-examples of the targeted replacement behavior.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete the goal-setting and self-monitoring tasks.
options.D: Assign reflective journal entries in which the student is encouraged to write or draw freely about their experience.
